articles.title: OpenAI seems to be silently re-enabling model training on Codex chats
articles.title_ja: OpenAI seems to be silently re-enabling model training on Codex chats
articles.summary_ja:
Title: OpenAI seems to be silently re-enabling model training on Codex chats
HN text: My company is pretty paranoid about leaking IP to the frontier labs through prompts, so we've all been diligent about disabling data sharing in Codex/Claude Code/etc. But yesterday my coworkers and I noticed that the setting had been silently reenabled in Codex. None of us knowingly opted back in. You can check your settings here: https://chatgpt.com/settings/data-controls. Look for "Improve the model for everyone". Curious if this is an isolated issue or something more widespread. EDIT: looks like this has been noted before https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49643556 EDIT: apparently you can also turn off data sharing here: https://privacy.openai.com/policies?modal=take-control

Article text:
Dawei Sun Blog
About
From Words to Waypoints: Teaching a Small LLM to Plan for Robots
Large language models are increasingly asked to act as the high-level planner of a robot: given a task in words or in a formal language, decide where to go, in which order, and when. For tasks written in temporal logic, the classical approach is to encode the whole problem as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) and hand it to a solver. That works, but it can take a very long time, and the cost grows quickly with the length of the task and the number of conditions. A MILP solver is a powerful but blind search: every operator, at every time step, becomes a set of binary variables and constraints, and the solver has no notion of…
